consultations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: feedback
consultations.section: Uncountable response-information sense1 and selected topic, lines103-139; electrical sense2 line142
consultations.finding: The selected feedback concerns advice, evaluation or information about work and its usefulness. It is uncountable, with give/receive and on/from patterns. B2 appears on the selected suggestions/advice topic. Electrical noise and returning a signal are separate meanings.
consultations.limits: AI author consultation only. No dictionary text, audio, images or license acquired. Selected-sense labels are literal observations, separate from editorial course levels. consultations.section: COBUILD sense1 lines222-228 and electrical sense2 lines230-231; British contrasts lines264-306

consultations.title: Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary: address
consultations.section: Postal details sense1 lines109-146; computing sense2 lines150-161 and speech sense3 lines162-176
consultations.finding: The postal details identify a home/work location and where mail can be sent. No postal CEFR label was visible. A1 belongs to the computing phone/email/internet topic, not the selected postal passage. The details can be given or spoken; defining them as necessarily written is unnecessarily narrow. Mailing address is especially North American and postal address usually British, without restricting the headword.

consultations.section: Selected time-zone noun lines101-110
consultations.finding: The regional-time sense carries B2. The inspected definition uses a simplified 24-area, one-hour-neighbor model. That detail is not adopted as a universal factual claim; the current same-standard-time region definition is sufficient. No actual date, offset, daylight-saving rule or scheduled conversion is validated.

consultations.section: COBUILD lines218-230 and British regional standard time lines238-244
consultations.finding: The headword allows time zone and time-zone; no selected CEFR is visible. The British entry directly supports a region using a shared standard time. The accompanying simplified 24-zone description does not justify assuming every civil offset is a whole hour or remains constant through the year. Keep the existing spaced answer only.
